significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling—“the more tokens an entity name is split into, the harder it is for the model to retrieve facts”—together with a form-(ii) mechanism in which the impairment is “causally localized to early-layer subject-token aggregation.” This would predict factual-retrieval differences among entities within the same language rather than merely redescribe the cross-language gaps documented by X-FACTR (Jiang et al., 2020), and it would connect that behavioral law to a specific processing stage. It establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanism; the negative branch would rule out fragmentation as an independent explanation after language and resource controls and, separately, reject the proposed early-aggregation account. True and false outcomes are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: replacing these specific token-count and aggregation claims with the generic multilingual-representation topic would not retain this level of constraint.

reach.justification: The principal handles are the measurable “subject token count (fertility)” as a predictor and the interventions “subject-representation pooling / retokenization”; fertility is ex ante because it can flag vulnerable entity queries before retrieval, while pooling or retokenization supplies an actionable mitigation. After tokenizer-specific recalibration, the claimed monotonic relation still predicts that more fragmented names will suffer worse factual access, so the substantive conclusion transfers rather than merely providing a procedure for rediscovery. The asserted scope spans languages, resource levels, and factual-retrieval cases, although it does not state a quantitative effect size or invariance across architectures and training regimes; likely downstream users include multilingual-model auditors and developers screening tokenizers or retrieval reliability. The topic-substitution check passes: the generic topic supplies neither this pre-query fragmentation signal nor the associated mitigation, so the reach comes from the claim-specific handles.
